No verdict, gate, loop condition, threshold or bound changed — asserted.

Suite count reported before and after.

constraints: RULED BEHAVIOUR CHANGE (Ruling D24). Record the ruling in the notebook before implementing it.

READ THE PREMISE FROM THE TRACE FIRST: quote what the rework iteration's implement call actually received. If it already received the review findings, the premise is wrong — say so and return NO_ACTION with the artifact.

THE MINIMAL CHANGE: on a review_rework_loop iteration, pass the incoming review's findings (rework_review's block or its dissent) and the review_clean gate's on_fail_reason into the implement phase's context. Do not change the build_loop's first iteration — it has no prior failure to carry.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE -062 CHANGE, which is CARRIED and unexecuted. If -062 has executed, extend its plumbing to this loop rather than writing a second one — the two loops run the identical eight-node body and should share one mechanism. State which path you took.
Do NOT change verdict semantics, gate routing, loop exit conditions, thresholds or bounds. Only what the implement phase is told, on a rework iteration.
Do NOT change what rework_review concludes. Nor review_fold's fold. The fix is what implement RECEIVES, not what any judge decides.

EXTEND THE -051/-054 HARNESS: a case where build_loop passes, review says ship=false, rework receives the findings and the re-run converges to review_fold.passed. Assert what the rework implement call was passed — quote it. A test that asserts only that the run completed does not test this ruling.
REPLAY THE -049 TRACE's iteration sequence through the changed code where possible, or state plainly that the live trace cannot be replayed provider-free and why.
Prove it by breaking it: remove the plumbing and show the assertion fail.
Keep the diff small. Suite reported before and after.
